headline: Brazil-Germany World Cup rematch? Remembering the 7-1 nightmare.
summary: The football world speculates on a potential clash between Brazil and Germany in the upcoming World Cup, bringing back memories of their historic 7-1 semi-final match. Fans are eager to see if Brazil can seek redemption.
details: The 2014 FIFA World Cup semi-final saw Germany deliver a stunning 7-1 defeat to host nation Brazil, a result that shocked the football world. This historic match took place in Belo Horizonte and ended Brazil's hopes of winning the tournament on home soil.

The loss was a deeply traumatic experience for Brazilian fans and players, marking one of the most significant upsets in World Cup history. Germany, on the other hand, advanced to win the tournament, cementing their place in football lore.

As a new World Cup approaches, speculation is rife about a potential rematch between these two football giants. Fans and pundits are already discussing the possibility of Brazil getting a chance to avenge their devastating 2014 loss.

Such an encounter would undoubtedly be one of the most anticipated matches of the tournament, carrying immense emotional weight for both teams. It would offer Brazil a chance at redemption and Germany an opportunity to reassert dominance.

headline_marked: Brazil President Lula jokes [[Neymar is doing 'home office']] at World Cup due to injury
headline: Brazil President Lula jokes Neymar is doing 'home office' at World Cup due to injury
summary: Brazilian President Lula da Silva playfully remarked that injured star Neymar is doing 'home office' for the national team during the World Cup, drawing attention to his absence from recent matches.
details: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva jokingly referred to star footballer Neymar as the "world's first home office player" during a public event. The remark came as Neymar is sidelined from the World Cup due to a calf injury, missing crucial matches for the national team.

Lula, a political rival of former President Jair Bolsonaro (whom Neymar supports), made the comment playfully at a cancer treatment investment event in Belo Horizonte. He asked a child who Brazil's best player was, and after the child said Neymar, Lula quipped about his absence.

Neymar has been in rehabilitation for a month due to a calf injury. He missed Brazil's first match against Morocco, which ended in a 1-1 draw, and will also be absent from the second match against Haiti.

While other team members traveled to Philadelphia for the Haiti match, Neymar remained at the team's base camp in New Jersey, USA. He is expected to return to the field for Brazil's third group stage match against Scotland after completing his rehabilitation.
